claims.text: The initial Mg-containing high-entropy alloy is a single-phase, homogeneous metastable solid solution.
During an isothermal hold at 500 °C, the alloy remains a homogeneous solid solution until a critical threshold is reached.
Crossing the critical threshold causes Mg to segregate from the metastable matrix.
Mg segregation nucleates Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
The formation of Mg-rich intermetallic phases produces new XRD diffraction peaks.
Electron microscopy and EDS will detect local chemical heterogeneities associated with the ordered Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
Thermal energy at 500 °C eventually overcomes the kinetic barrier to Mg segregation.
Mg segregation triggers nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
The intermetallic transformation produces compositional heterogeneity in the microstructure.
Transformation-induced compositional heterogeneities may stabilize protective oxide layers at high temperatures.
Transformation-induced compositional heterogeneities may create sites that degrade room-temperature corrosion resistance.
A distinct onset time for the appearance of Mg-rich intermetallic diffraction peaks will occur during the 500 °C hold.
The microstructural transformation will correlate with measurable changes in corrosion performance.
The microstructural transformation will correlate with measurable changes in high-temperature oxidation performance.
The initial state contains no detectable Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
Exposure at 500 °C beyond the critical onset time will cause intermetallic formation to significantly affect corrosion and oxidation behavior.
The hypothesis is falsified if no Mg-rich intermetallic diffraction peaks appear within the expected experimental timeframe.
The hypothesis is falsified if emergent Mg-rich intermetallic phases do not correlate with changes in corrosion and oxidation performance.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes a critical thermal activation threshold, but the temperature is fixed at 500 °C and the boundary is subsequently defined as a critical cumulative exposure time. This conflates a thermal threshold with an unquantified incubation-time threshold.
